clue.text: You can get bogged down in this pile of paper about meeting

definitions.text: You can get bogged down in this

indicators.note: about means going round, so the paper pile wraps around the meeting

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
an AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: An office worker drowning under a heap of paperwork for an upcoming meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase is a whole-sentence definition of a bog: QU(AGM)IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is a soft boggy area of land where feet sink and people get stuck.

clue.text: It's unlucky, being drawn out at random

indicators.note: at random says the letters are drawn in no set order and must be reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans their luck at being picked out in a random draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfortunate or inconvenient, an old-fashioned sense close to ill-starred or unlucky.

clue.text: Novel way to interrupt mockery

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to guy is to ridicule, so guying is mockery
a manner is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone finds a new method of breaking up teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the definition: GUY(MANNER)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Mannering is an 1815 historical book by Sir Walter Scott, one of his Waverley series.

clue.text: I am old, sitting around in thought

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: sitting around means placed round something, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: aged means old
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly person sits musing, lost in their thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in thought' looks like one phrase meaning pensive, but 'in' belongs to the wordplay and 'thought' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought here is a past participle: something thought up has been dreamt up in the mind.

clue.text: Oriental is a point behind

parts.note: E for east, one point of the compass
astern means behind a ship

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a person from the Orient trails by a point in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The natural split is EAST + ERN, but 'behind' is ASTERN, after the single compass point E.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is an old word for things belonging to Asia, the lands lying to the east.

clue.text: Horse taken in finished up drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top
taken in means swallowed or held inside something else

parts.note: gone means over and done with
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A horse is brought in after finishing and gets a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means read from the bottom; the horse goes inside after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a beverage of beaten eggs, milk and sugar, often with spirits added.

clue.text: Some pupils to abandon philosophy school

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and into the next two

explanation.surface: A group of students drop out of their philosophy course.
explanation.walkthrough: pupilS TO Abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoa was the porch in Athens where Zeno taught, so it names the Stoic school of thinkers.

clue.text: Not just Welsh furlong has to be converted

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for Welsh

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that the Welsh furlong is not merely a local measure but must be changed into another unit.

explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair or right, so something not just is unfair, unlawful or wrongful.

clue.text: More imposing venue for the Masters, by the sound of it

parts.note: Augusta National in Georgia hosts the Masters golf tournament

explanation.surface: A golfer praises the grandeur of the Masters course.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, Augusta and auguster sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: August means majestic and inspiring awe, so its comparative describes something grander or more dignified.

clue.text: Guy in residence

second meaning: a period of living somewhere, as in a hotel

explanation.surface: A man is at home in his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but here it is a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a guy and this word name a supporting rope on a ship; a short time spent living somewhere is also called this.

clue.text: Could an estate, short of oil initially, produce full power?

parts.note: might is the past of may, meaning could
taken as written

parts.note: the opening letter of oil

explanation.walkthrough: DOMAIN loses its O to become DMAIN, giving MIGHT + AN + DMAIN.

clue.text: Urge them on to reform the language that comes naturally

clue.text: Piece, a musical composition, featuring one note

clue.text: Verbally cancel without delay

explanation.definitionFit: Right off is an informal idiom meaning immediately, at once, straight away.

clue.text: Append finis to a list of omissions

finis is Latin for the end
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor tacks 'The End' onto a list of things left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items supplied afterwards to make good what a book or document left out.

clue.text: Small creature having to run away, a gazelle, perhaps

explanation.surface: A little animal bolts, like a gazelle fleeing danger.

clue.text: Badger has two bases

clue.text: Expecting some fortification

clue.text: … enlightenment that may be observed
